title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the notation and the conference title (PD de Rham complex). S is a graded ring, possibly a symmetric or divided-power algebra. M_N is a category of graded S-modules truncated in degrees <= N, or more generally truncated between N' and N. tau_N (and tau_{N,N'}) is the truncation functor. phi_N (and phi_{N',N}) is its right adjoint, Hom(tau_N M, P) = Hom(M, phi_N P). phi_N is left exact, so one studies its right derived functors R^n phi_N.

Example M = S[-i] (free rank-one module shifted to degree i). By adjunction:
- K_i(R*phi_N P), the degree-i component, is RHom(tau_N(S[-i]), P).
- Since tau_N(S[-i]) = (tau_{N-i}S)[-i], this equals RHom((tau_{N-i}S)[-i], P), i.e. a graded RHom^i(tau_{N-i}S, P).
- Hence (R^n phi_N(tau_N P))_i = Ext^n((tau_{N-i}S)[-i], P).

NB: the same holds for phi_{N',N} (N' <= N) provided i >= N'; for i < N' the component is 0.

Crossed-out attempt: for P in the essential image of phi_{N',N}, i.e. P = phi tau P, one would have R^n phi(tau P) = 0 for n > 0, i.e. Ext^n(tau_{N-i}S[-i], P) = 0 for i >= N', n > 0. It is abandoned, rightly so, since an object lying in the essential image need not be acyclic.

Replacement lemma. Let C be abelian and i: C -> M_{N0'} an exact functor with i(C) inside the essential image of phi_{N0',N}, i.e. i = phi tau i. Claim: (R^n phi_{N0',N})(tau_{N,N0'} o i) = 0 for n > 0. Argument:
- R*i = 0 in positive degrees because i is exact.
- R*i = R*(phi tau i), and R*(phi tau i) = (R*phi)(tau i) because tau o i is exact.

Purpose: to get acyclicity of truncation/extension functors on suitable subcategories. This is presumably needed to compare truncated (order-N) data with untruncated data in the PD-de Rham setting, e.g. modules over the PD envelopes of order N.
errors: The final step R*(phi o G) = (R*phi) o G for an exact G = tau o i is not justified by exactness of G alone. One needs G to send injectives (or enough objects) to phi-acyclics, e.g. G has an exact left adjoint, or an effaceability argument for the delta-functor (R^n phi) o G. As written the proof has a gap; the conclusion may still hold in the intended concrete situation.
The crossed-out NB (an object in the essential image is phi-acyclic) is false in general. Grothendieck crossed it out, correctly.

ideas.what: Computing the graded components of the derived functors of the right adjoint of degree-truncation via Ext from truncated free modules: (R^n phi_N P)_i = Ext^n((tau_{N-i}S)[-i], P)
ideas.modern_name: derived right adjoint of restriction/truncation; adjunction computation of derived functors on graded modules

ideas.what: Acyclicity lemma: an exact functor landing in the essential image of a left-exact right adjoint yields vanishing higher derived functors on the composite
ideas.modern_name: acyclicity / composite derived functors (Grothendieck spectral sequence situation)
ideas.where_published: Tohoku paper (general composite-functor theory); this specific lemma unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Routine homological-algebra bookkeeping (adjunction, truncation, Ext) in service of the PD de Rham notes. The general lemma has a small gap and nothing appears novel or absent from the literature. The neighbouring pages are unrelated SGA 7 IX text.
